inspiration: Aggro is a sorted list of threat values per creature, sorted high to low, and the creature picks the top entry that is not a second-choice target. Keep the order-then-filter pick; add our own dodge and guard threat rules. Refs: src/game/References/ThreatManager.cpp lines 410-413, 440-470.

A hit's threat is a flat base value scaled by spell threat mods, a crit multiplier and then the target's total threat modifier, applied in a fixed order. Keep the fixed order and the flat-first rule; add guard and parry as multipliers. Ref: ThreatManager.cpp lines 73-99.

Taunt copies the current leader's threat onto the taunter, but only when the taunter is below it, and it is a temporary value that fades. A cheap way to swap aggro that never overshoots. Ref: ThreatManager.cpp lines 723-732; UnitThreat.cpp line 164 (stunned or dead units cannot taunt).
Loot is a store of entries; a group entry picks one winner by roll, and each entry has its own roll. Keep the one-of-N group pick. Refs: src/game/Object/LootMgr.cpp lines 368 and 1209.

Creature behaviour is written as event rows in a table (on hit, on health band, on timer) rather than in code; the doc describes the event parameters and actions. Good for our boss phases if the rows stay in zone data. Ref: extra/doc/EventAI.md (intro at line 5; event tables from line 127).

Scripts and text tables are documented as separate guides (SD3 text tables, SQL guide), so the data author has a short format contract. Good template for our catalogue fields. Ref: extra/doc/SD3_Text-tables.md, extra/doc/SD3_SQL_guide.md (not read beyond names).

briefs.label: Pull-the-aggro swap (enemy target choice)
briefs.why: A boss that shifts target to the most threatening fighter, with a visible tell, makes many-on-one fights readable. Works at 375 wide with a single ring on the new target.
briefs.keep: a sorted threat list; the top non-second-choice target wins; taunt copies the leader value and fades
briefs.change: a 3-attacker cap (our MAX_ATTACKERS); a swap tell (ring and sound) when the target changes; guard and parry feed threat

briefs.label: Group loot pick (drop ceremony)
briefs.why: One-of-N group entries give a drop moment with a clear winner; the reveal can be the loot beat for a fight.
briefs.keep: a group entry picks one winner; each entry carries its own roll
briefs.change: a visible roll reveal with rarity sound; our own item groups; a 'contested' beat when two players want the same item

briefs.label: Boss phase rows (creature behaviour as data)
briefs.why: Behaviour written as event rows lets a designer add a phase without code. Phases with a visible bar work at 375 wide.
briefs.keep: behaviour as rows of event, condition and action; a timer event and a health-band event
briefs.change: our event names and phase bar; a finisher beat on the last phase; no SQL, the rows live in our zone data
